purpose: Original editorial grounding aids, not publisher wording, mandatory fact lists, a model abstract, or a comparison verdict.

abstract.reader_question: How can low-rank processing coexist with full-parameter learning?
abstract.expected_relation: Compress gradient statistics rather than freezing weights, and refresh projection subspaces so successive updates are not confined to one fixed low-rank region.

abstract.reader_question: Which experimental settings delimit the memory-efficiency claim?
abstract.expected_relation: Bound savings by optimizer, projection rank, per-layer updates, and token batch; keep pretraining quality and small-batch device feasibility as distinct evaluations.

methods.reader_question: What operation produces a memory-efficient weight update?
methods.expected_relation: Project gradients into a compact space, maintain optimizer statistics there, lift the processed update back to weight space, and periodically recompute the projector.

methods.reader_question: Which assumptions and implementation choices limit the theoretical argument?
methods.expected_relation: Keep conditional low-rank and fixed-projection convergence statements separate from adaptive-optimizer practice and the subspace-refresh trade-off.

results.reader_question: What joint trade-off is tested by compression and refresh?
results.expected_relation: Read perplexity and fine-tuning scores alongside optimizer memory, throughput, rank, refresh frequency, and training length instead of treating memory savings alone as success.

results.reader_question: How far do the 7B and fine-tuning measurements generalize?
results.expected_relation: Separate a single-trial multi-GPU quality run from low-token-batch single-device memory feasibility, and retain task-specific comparisons that differ from aggregate trends.
